title: Intermittency analysis in relativistic hydrodynamic simulations of heavy-ion collision at FAIR energies
text:
Abstract
In this paper, we present comprehensive results on intermittency using the Scaled Factorial Moment (SFM) technique in Au + Au collisions in the FAIR energy range of 2–12A GeV in pseudorapidity , azimuthal, and pseudorapidity-azimuthal spaces. The simulations are performed with a hybrid version of the Ultra-relativistic Quantum Molecular Dynamics (UrQMD) event generator. Three alternative equations of state (EoS) are employed to investigate the intermittency within the hydrodynamic scenario, namely pure Hadron Gas (HG), Chiral + HG, and Bag Model EoS. In both one and two-dimensional spaces and at all beam energies, a weak intermittent type of emission has been seen for Chiral+HG EoS. In contrast, a strong intermittent kind of emission is observed for Bag Model EoS. The incident beam energy dependency of intermittency has also been investigated. The strength of the intermittency is seen to diminish with increasing beam energy.

Profile
I’m a software engineer and data analyst with 8+ years building Python and C++ software, automated QA frameworks, and reliable data-processing pipelines within large international research collaborations (CBM/FAIR, GSI Helmholtz Centre, and Goethe University Frankfurt).
I turn complex, large-scale datasets into reliable, decision-ready insights through well-engineered, reproducible workflows — and I’m now focused on software engineering and data roles in industry.


What I do

Design and ship maintainable Python / C++ software, with automated testing and CI/CD.
Build data-quality and validation frameworks that catch regressions automatically.
Turn large, messy datasets into validated insights, dashboards, and reports.
Optimise performance — e.g. an 8× runtime reduction on a geometry-processing pipeline, with full accuracy preserved.



Core skills

Languages: Python, C++, SQL, R
Data & analysis: pandas, NumPy, statistical analysis, data validation & cleaning, Tableau
Software & DevOps: Git, Docker, CMake, CI/CD, automated testing, Linux / HPC
Domain: scientific computing, detector simulation, large-scale data pipelines (ROOT)
